official_tier: Permit to keep protected wildlife
notes: nt.gov.au says you need a permit to keep a crocodile but names no species or conditions. The two NT species are C. johnstoni and C. porosus; check with PWCNT whether both can be kept privately. Source: https://www.nt.gov.au/environment/animals/keeping-wildlife-as-pets/keeping-crocodiles

tier: NT natives: Permit required. Non-NT reptiles: Permit required, case by case. Non-NT frogs and turtles: Not permitted
official_tier: Permit to keep protected or prohibited wildlife (TPWC Act 1976 ss 43, 52, 55); prohibited-entrant rules
notes: NT has no published positive list of keepable non-venomous species and no tiered licences. Rules: (a) every native NT reptile/frog not exempt needs a permit to keep protected wildlife, bought from a lawful permitted source, applied for within 7 days of purchase (no frogs are exempt); (b) Australian reptiles not native to the NT are prohibited entrants, which need an import permit plus a keep permit, assessed case by case; (c) frogs not native to the NT are illegal, and turtle imports are never permitted (even NT-origin animals); (d) exotics can't be kept privately (red-eared slider, axolotl specifically banned); (e) venomous snakes not permitted: Austrelaps, Hoplocephalus, Notechis, Tropidechis carinatus, Rhinoplocephalus nigrescens. Sources: https://nt.gov.au/environment/animals/wildlife-permits/keeping-protected-prohibited-wildlife ; https://nt.gov.au/environment/animals/wildlife-permits/prohibited-wildlife ; https://nt.gov.au/environment/animals/keeping-wildlife-as-pets/keeping-snakes/permits-for-venomous-snakes
